svg.title: Data Connectors
svg.desc: Data Connectors: registry matrix, 11 rows by 4 columns. ?data= <provider>:<id>.<metric>. Columns: SOURCE, IDENTIFIER, METRICS, KIND. Full data in hw:payload.

hw:zone.reason: var() does not resolve in an SVG presentation attribute, so this paint is decided at compose time

hw:reasoning.hw:intent: One 900-wide matrix carrying BOTH faces: the light face in the base scope, the dark face behind prefers-color-scheme, so a single file reads correctly in a light README and a dark one without a second asset or a picture-element pair.
hw:reasoning.hw:approach: The solved geometry is emitted once — column widths, the 140px label floor, the 40px row pitch, the 33px masthead — and only the chromatic layer forks: the genome block is rescoped from `svg, :root` to the artifact's own #uid selector, and a sparse far-palette block restates the same --dna-* roles inside the media query. Contrast parity, not a lightness mirror, picks the far values, so the ink holds its 12.0 floor against either ground.
hw:reasoning.hw:tradeoffs: The #uid scope is what makes two faces fit in one file, and it costs the global `svg, :root` block — a host page can no longer retheme the artifact by setting --dna-* on an ancestor, only on the artifact itself. Gradient stops and filter floods cannot read a custom property at all, so those flip through paired CSS rules instead; the file is larger than either baked face for exactly that duplication.
